All stat sections below reflect this window (overtime plays, if any, only count toward Full Game). The drive chart always shows the full game. Loading…
Percentiles (in the Overall panel) are per-game, computed across FBS-vs-FBS matchups in the Week 1–2 dataset (~198 team-games) — a small early-season sample, so treat them as directional. Items marked * use a formula rather than a provider field: Line Yards / Highlight Yards follow the standard Football Outsiders weighted-credit formula; Available Yards % excludes drives starting inside the 10; Havoc Plays, TFLs, Passes Defensed and Fumbles Forced are parsed from play-text phrases ("broken up by," "forced by") and will undercount. Explosive plays use the 10+ rush / 15+ pass yardage definition used throughout this dashboard. Expected Points / Expected Turnovers are omitted — the source data has no EPA on penalty or special-teams plays, and turnover luck requires a predictive model we don't have.
Methodology. *Yards per play leaves out every play snapped at or inside the opponent's 5-yard line (on both offense and defense), inferred as Distance needed for a first down reaching past the goal line (no native goal-to-go flag in this data) -- a compressed field caps how many yards a play can gain; the plays and yards still count everywhere else (totals, EPA, success rate, explosives). Plays from scrimmage include rushes, pass attempts (completions, incompletions, sacks, interceptions) and live-ball penalty plays; kickoffs, punts, field goals, timeouts and dead-ball ("no play") penalties are excluded. Explosive = a run of 10+ yards or a completion of 15+ yards. EPA figures use each play's provider-computed Predicted Points Added (Ppa); EPA/pass includes sack plays, EPA/rush is every rush including scrambles and designed QB runs (the data has no separate scramble tag). 3rd/4th down conversions are inferred from "1ST DOWN"/"TOUCHDOWN" markers in the play text, plus the play's own type for touchdowns the text doesn't spell out (e.g. "...for a TD (Kicker Kick)"). Early-down success rate (1st/2nd down) counts a play as successful if it gains at least 50% (1st down) or 70% (2nd down) of the needed yardage, or a 3rd/4th down snap if it converts. Series conversion rate = share of offensive series (each new set of downs) that end in another 1st down or a touchdown -- reconstructed play-by-play from Down/Distance/YardsToGoal and the same "1ST DOWN"/"TOUCHDOWN" text markers, (plus each play's own type for touchdowns the text doesn't spell out), since this provider has no native series field; a series abandoned via kneel-down before being resolved (clock-killing a lead) is excluded from both sides' denominators, the same way a punt, missed field goal or turnover on downs counts as a failed series. Defensive series conversion is the same rate for opponents (lower is better). Ranks are out of — FBS teams across the two weeks of data loaded. Records reflect only the games included in this dataset, not full-season record.
